item: The layers against a cross-site POST are stated in SECURITY.md, FastAPI is floored at 0.133.0 and the JSON-route 422 is pinned (audit 0.5.0 item 35, options 1+2)
refs: PR #1517; coordinator 26 Oct 21:51: ship options 1+2 of the item 35 proposal; R252 proposal item 35; Opus read q-item35-OPUS_READ.md and Plan's registry read (floor 0.132.0 unreachable under starlette>=1.5.0) folded; version-coupling rule
summary: docs/SECURITY.md now states the layers in the order a request meets them (Origin/Referer 403 as the OUTER middleware, then the Host allow-set 421, then FastAPI's 422 on a required JSON body) and what none covers: the layer-3 coverage measured from the OpenAPI schema (317 state-changing operations on 2026-10-26, 148 with no body, 11 with an optional one, plus six raw-body modules), side-effect GETs (/api/database/backup partly closed by its own R214 guard, /api/geo/downloads/size a proposal), browsers that send no Origin/Referer. pyproject floors fastapi at 0.133.0 (was >=0.110; the lock pins 0.138.0): the first-proposed 0.132.0 requires starlette<1.0.0 beside the app's starlette>=1.5.0, so pip answers ResolutionImpossible, while 0.133.0 resolves. Registry entry fastapi-strict-content-type (floor 0.133.0, verified 0.162.0 = newest on PyPI 2026-10-26) and a coupling test in tests/test_external_freshness.py. tests/test_security_hardening.py pins that POST /api/newsletters/remove-imported answers 422 model_attributes_type to text/plain, text/plain;charset, form-urlencoded, multipart and no Content-Type, and reaches the handler (400) as application/json. MEASURED on unpacked wheels, the floor pair fastapi 0.133.0 + starlette 1.5.0 passing all 7 rows: 0.131.0 fails exactly ONE row (no Content-Type is parsed as JSON); text/plain, form-urlencoded and multipart were already 422 there. Options 3 (Sec-Fetch-Site in the middleware) and 4 (own Content-Type middleware) not built.
